Revision 1.128 participant; environment roster row added in the period-4 wave. Wikidata Q97585539 confirmed by QLever on 2026-10-23 (the sheet's unreviewed 1.128 match).

proposed_edges.relationship: Conservation as dispossession: Indian removal made the 'uninhabited wilderness' of Yellowstone, Glacier and Yosemite (Spence 1999); the Stoney excluded from Banff for game, sport and assimilation (Binnema and Niemi 2006); northern game laws as state authority over hunting cultures (Sandlos 2007)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Spence's OUP abstract read; the Binnema–Niemi and Piper–Sandlos abstracts read; Sandlos's UBC Press description read. Warren and Jacoby are not on this edge: their books are unread and no reader read here states a dispossession argument for them (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md §§6–7). Source strand environment/conservation_dispossession; target strand indigenous/land. Overlaps edge_696 (indigenous ↔ environment, a comparison through Huggins, Bullard, Cronon and Carruthers), which stays.

proposed_edges.relationship: Canadian environmental histories of the fur-trade and northern worlds: the pemmican market that 'nearly wiped out the Canadian bison herds north of the Missouri River' (Colpitts 2014); ecological imperialism as 'a broken frontier' in the North (Piper and Sandlos 2007); Dene and Inuit hunters against conservationists (Sandlos 2007)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Publisher descriptions and the 2007 abstract read; bodies unread (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md §6.3). Reduced strength. Source strand environment/canadian_environmental_history; target strand native_newcomer/fur_trade_national_economy.

proposed_edges.relationship: Capital against the species: Malm's Fossil Capital (2016) holds that 'steam offered neither cheaper nor more abundant energy' but control over labour; Moore's Capitalism in the Web of Life (2015) and Stoll's 'A Metabolism of Society' (2014) ask what capitalism is for environmental historians; Worster had made agricultural capitalism 'the decisive factor' (1979)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Malm's publisher page read; Moore metadata only; Stoll by chapter title in the Oxford Handbook contents; Worster's phrase as recorded in the graph's existing records (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md §9). A teaching comparison, not a reception claim. Source strand environment/anthropocene_climate.

row.context: Conservation, dams and relocation as histories of the Canadian state and of 'the scales of justice' at which environmental change is apprehended (2006–19); asked the field in 2014 to connect with the world. Books known by publisher description; the 2007 abstract read.
row.works: States of Nature (2006); 'Disturbing the Peace' (2007); 'Missed Connections' (2014); Moved by the State (2019)

row.context: Industry in the subarctic lakes, 1921–60, 'a seam in the Canadian interior where industrial economies took root'; with Sandlos, ecological imperialism as 'a broken frontier' in the North, where 'the broad ecological transformation' of the south never came. Description and abstract read; bodies unread.
row.works: The Industrial Transformation of Subarctic Canada (2009); with John Sandlos, 'A Broken Frontier' (2007)

row.context: Atlantic Canada's national parks (2001); NiCHE's director in its SSHRC-cluster years; co-editor of the 2007 Canadian number of Environmental History and of Method and Meaning (2009). Book unread; publisher page unreachable.
row.works: Natural Selections (2001); Environmental History 12:4 (2007, ed. with Evenden); Method and Meaning in Canadian Environmental History (2009, ed. with Turkel)

row.context: Geographer and general editor of UBC Press's Nature | History | Society series ('the interface between nature and society'); wrote the 2007 synthesis Canada and Arctic North America (unread) and in 2003 called the field 'undeveloped in this country, compared with the United States'.
row.works: Canada and Arctic North America (2007); series forewords (2006–)

row.context: Game laws, parks and sanctuaries in the Northwest Territories 'helped the state assert authority over traditional hunting cultures' (2007; CHA Clio and FHS Weyerhaeuser awards); Jacoby called it 'a powerful new interpretation'. Description read; body unread.
row.works: Hunters at the Margin (2007); with Liza Piper, 'A Broken Frontier' (2007)

row.context: The Fraser as 'a river basin where development decisions did not ultimately dam the river, but rather conserved its salmon' (2004); urban rivers compared across Europe and North America (2012); co-editor of the 2007 Canadian number. Descriptions read; bodies unread.
row.works: Fish versus Power (2004); Urban Rivers (2012, ed. with Castonguay)

row.context: The pemmican trade as a food market that 'nearly wiped out the Canadian bison herds north of the Missouri River' (2014). Publisher description only.
row.works: Pemmican Empire (2014)

row.context: Embodied, sensory histories of megaprojects and environmental change in Canada, 1953–2003 (edge_963); the row places her in the Canadian field's cohort of the 2000s.
row.works: Sensing Changes (2010); 'Smells Like?' (2006)

row.context: World environmental history of the twentieth century (2000; WHA and Weyerhaeuser prizes), a survey of the field's 'nature and culture' (2003), the Anthropocene since 1945 (2016); ASEH president; told the AHA in 2020 that the field 'stands to be disrupted, and with luck enhanced, more than most'. The 2000 and 2016 books unread.
row.works: Something New Under the Sun (2000); 'Observations on the Nature and Culture of Environmental History' (2003); with Engelke, The Great Acceleration (2016)

row.context: Surveyed the field for the JAH in 2013: environmental historians had 'replaced the once-firm categories of nature and culture with various approaches to environmental hybridity', a turn 'analytically essential' yet leaving the field 'at a moral crossroads' (the editors' summary; the essay is unread); succeeded Cronon as Weyerhaeuser series editor (2014).
row.works: 'The World with Us: The State of American Environmental History' (2013); Driven Wild (2002)

row.context: Cronon's student at Yale; the 'hidden history' of conservation as squatters, poachers and thieves (2001; Marsh and Littleton-Griswold prizes). Book unread; known through the CV and Crossref.
row.works: Crimes against Nature (2001)

row.context: Indian removal from Yellowstone, Glacier and Yosemite as the making of 'uninhabited wilderness' (1999). Abstract read; body unread.
row.works: Dispossessing the Wilderness (1999)

row.context: Wilderness activist who answered the academic critics: the 'Received Wilderness Idea' of 'Baird Callicott, Bill Cronon and other postmodern deconstructionist scholars' is 'a straw dog; it does not exist on the ground' (1999/2000; read in full), against 'the Real Wilderness Idea' that built the National Wilderness Preservation System.
row.works: 'Wilderness Areas for Real' (1998); 'The Real Wilderness Idea' (2000)

row.context: Co-editor of the anthology; his own position and the editors' introduction were not read. Foreman groups him with Cronon among academic critics of wilderness.
row.works: The Great New Wilderness Debate (ed. with Michael P. Nelson, 1998)

row.context: Asked whether nature has agency or agency has a nature in the 2005 anniversary forum and urged 'Furthering the Environmental Turn' in the 2013 forum; disease as environmental history (2006, 2014). Metadata only.
row.works: 'The Agency of Nature or the Nature of Agency?' (2005); Inescapable Ecologies (2006); 'Furthering the Environmental Turn' (2013)

row.context: Edited the Oxford Handbook (2014), whose abstract holds the field 'widely recognized within the mainstream of academic history' since the early 1980s and whose introduction 'focuses on the integration of the insights of environmental history with a host of other subfields'; his 2013 survey is read.
row.works: The Oxford Handbook of Environmental History (ed., 2014); 'From the Periphery to the Center' (2013)

row.context: Fossil Capital (2016): 'steam offered neither cheaper nor more abundant energy' but control over labour; read on its cover as an answer to the 'Anthropocene narrative'. Publisher page only.
row.works: Fossil Capital (2016)

row.context: With Fressoz, 'the first critical history of the Anthropocene', refusing 'the convenient view of a "human species" that upset the Earth system' (2013; English 2016). Publisher description only.
row.works: The Shock of the Anthropocene (2016, with Jean-Baptiste Fressoz)

row.context: With Bonneuil, 'the first critical history of the Anthropocene' (2013; English 2016). Publisher description only.
row.works: The Shock of the Anthropocene (2016, with Christophe Bonneuil)

row.context: Disease, climate and 'Canadian politics' in the loss of Indigenous life on the Plains (2013; GG History Award, Macdonald and Clio prizes); blurbed by McNeill. The settler-colonial reading is on settler_colonialism; its place in PhD bibliographies is in the conservation_dispossession strand.
row.works: Clearing the Plains (2013)

row.context: A world environmental history of the twentieth century (2000) and, with Engelke, of the Anthropocene since 1945 (2016): 'human dependence on fossil fuels inaugurated the Anthropocene'. Books unread.
row.works: Something New Under the Sun (2000); The Great Acceleration (2016)

row.context: Indian removal from Yellowstone, Glacier and Yosemite as the making of 'uninhabited wilderness' (1999): 'the early conception of the wilderness as the place where Indians lived (or should live)' gave way to its idealisation as empty. Abstract read.
row.works: Dispossessing the Wilderness (1999)

row.context: Conservation's 'hidden history' of squatters, poachers and thieves (2001); endorsed Sandlos's Canadian parallel. Book unread.
row.works: Crimes against Nature (2001)

row.context: Northern game laws, parks and sanctuaries as the state's authority over Dene and Inuit hunting cultures (2007). Description read.
row.works: Hunters at the Margin (2007)

new_people.label: J. R. McNeill
new_people.identity_note: American environmental historian (b. 1954), University Professor, Georgetown University; Something New Under the Sun (2000); president of the American Society for Environmental History; president of the American Historical Association 2019. Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not william_h_mcneill (Q1765863), his father.

new_people.label: Liza Piper
new_people.identity_note: Canadian environmental historian, University of Alberta; The Industrial Transformation of Subarctic Canada (2009); with John Sandlos, 'A Broken Frontier' (2007). Added in the period-4 wave (environment).

new_people.label: Graeme Wynn
new_people.identity_note: Canadian geographer and environmental historian (b. 1946), University of British Columbia; general editor of UBC Press's Nature | History | Society series; Canada and Arctic North America (2007). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not the rugby player Q5592427.

new_people.label: John Sandlos
new_people.identity_note: Environmental historian, Memorial University of Newfoundland; Hunters at the Margin (2007). Added in the period-4 wave (environment).

new_people.label: Matthew Evenden
new_people.identity_note: Canadian geographer and environmental historian (b. 1971), University of British Columbia; Fish versus Power (2004); co-editor of Urban Rivers (2012). Added in the period-4 wave (environment).

new_people.label: Alan MacEachern

new_people.label: George Colpitts

new_people.label: Paul S. Sutter

new_people.label: Karl Jacoby
new_people.identity_note: American historian (b. 1965), Columbia University; William Cronon's doctoral student at Yale (Ph.D. 1997); Crimes against Nature (2001). Added in the period-4 wave (environment).

new_people.identity_note: American historian; Dispossessing the Wilderness: Indian Removal and the Making of the National Parks (1999). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Ungrounded: only a peerage entry 'Mark Spence' (Q75533210) found on QLever (2026-10-23); not asserted.

new_people.label: Louis S. Warren
new_people.identity_note: American environmental historian; The Hunter's Game (1997); William Cronon's doctoral student at Yale (Ph.D. 1994). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not william_w_warren or jean_philippe_warren. Not queried on QLever this session.

new_people.label: Linda Nash
new_people.identity_note: American environmental historian (b. 1962), University of Washington; Inescapable Ecologies (2006); 'The Agency of Nature or the Nature of Agency?' (2005). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not roderick_nash.

new_people.identity_note: American wilderness activist (b. 1946), co-founder of Earth First! and chairman of The Wildlands Project; 'Wilderness Areas for Real' (1998) and 'The Real Wilderness Idea' (2000), replies to Cronon and Callicott. Added in the period-4 wave (environment).

new_people.identity_note: American environmental philosopher; co-editor with Michael P. Nelson of The Great New Wilderness Debate (1998); named by Foreman with Cronon as a 'deconstructionist'. Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not queried on QLever this session.

new_people.label: Michael P. Nelson
new_people.identity_note: Environmental philosopher; co-editor of The Great New Wilderness Debate (1998). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not queried on QLever this session.

new_people.identity_note: American environmental historian (Temple University at the time); editor of The Oxford Handbook of Environmental History (2014); 'From the Periphery to the Center' (2013). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not queried on QLever this session.

new_people.label: Theodore Binnema
new_people.identity_note: Canadian historian, University of Northern British Columbia; with Melanie Niemi, "'Let the Line Be Drawn Now'" (2006). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not queried on QLever this session.

new_people.identity_note: Co-author with Theodore Binnema of "'Let the Line Be Drawn Now'" (Environmental History, 2006). Added in the period-4 wave (environment). Not queried on QLever this session.
